summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -4 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar 0; brl −; risk 0; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +4.4%; weakest: Lean hogs -15.2%. Key releases ahead: US Core PPI m/m (11-13 8:30 AM ET); US PPI m/m (11-13 8:30 AM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.10% (-11 bp in a month), 2-year 4.86% (+7 bp); 2s10s curve +24 bp (-18 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.12% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.38 (+0.8% in a month, +5.2% YTD). USD/BRL 5.636 (+12.1% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.661 (-0.5%); USD/MXN 18.54 (+0.9%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -2.5% in a month (+9.9% YTD); VIX 20.0. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 88.89 $/bbl (-5.3% in a month), Brent 96.26, ULSD 4.314 $/gal (-9.2%), natural gas 3.24 (-9.0%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -8.3% in a month, Shanghai Composite -3.5%, Hang Seng -2.8%, yuan +0.5% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 8 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (24%); S&P GSCI -7.0% in a month; gold -5.6%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
